title: Vertical deleted-vertex reindexing of shuffle words with Koszul signs
statement:
For any set $S$, let $\mathbf Z[S]$ be the free $\mathbf Z$-module with basis $S$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; evaluated strings below can equivalently be read as basis symbols in the free module on strings of their length. Let $a,b\geq0$, $n=a+b$, and let $W_{a,b}$ be the finite set of words $w_0\cdots w_{n-1}$ with $a$ letters $H$ and $b$ letters $V$. Put $A_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=H\}$ and $B_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=V\}$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $I(w)=\#\{(r,s):r<s,\ w_r=V,\ w_s=H\}$ and $s(w)=(-1)^{I(w)}\in\mathbf Z$. For any sets $X,Y$ and sequences $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_a)$ in $X$, $v=(v_0,\ldots,v_b)$ in $Y$, write $z_{u,v}(w)=((u_{A_k(w)},v_{B_k(w)}))_{k=0}^n$ and let $d_k$ denote deletion of entry $k$ of a sequence. No distinctness of sequence entries is assumed.

Assume $b>0$. Let $V_{a,b}$ consist of the labeled pairs $(w,k)$ with $w\in W_{a,b}$ and either $k=0,w_0=V$, or $k=n,w_{n-1}=V$, or $0<k<n,w_{k-1}=w_k=V$. There is a bijection
$$\Phi_V:V_{a,b}\xrightarrow{\sim}\{0,\ldots,b\}\times W_{a,b-1}.$$
At an interior pair it is $(w,k)\mapsto(j,\bar w)$, where $j=B_k(w)$ and $\bar w$ replaces the two neighboring $V$ letters by one; here $1\leq j<b$. At $k=0$ it removes the initial $V$ and sets $j=0$; at $k=n$ it removes the terminal $V$ and sets $j=b$. Its inverse for $0<j<b$ splits the $j$-th $V$ of $\bar w$ (counted from one) into two $V$ letters and marks the intervening vertex; for $j=0,b$ it prepends or appends $V$ and marks that endpoint, respectively. If $\Phi_V(w,k)=(j,\bar w)$, then
$$d_kz_{u,v}(w)=z_{u,d_j v}(\bar w),\qquad s(w)(-1)^k=(-1)^{a+j}s(\bar w).$$
More precisely, at an interior pair, $i=A_k(w)$ satisfies $k=i+j$ and $I(w)=I(\bar w)+a-i$; at the initial endpoint $I(w)=I(\bar w)+a$; at the terminal endpoint $I(w)=I(\bar w)$ and $k=a+b$. These assertions include $b=1$ (only endpoint faces) and $a=0$. If $b=0$, the same labeled vertical set is empty.

proof.text: Suppose $b>0$, so $n>0$. At an interior vertical pair put $i=A_k(w)$ and $j=B_k(w)$. Every one of the first $k$ letters is either $H$ or $V$, so $k=i+j$. The letter at $k-1$ is $V$, hence $j\geq1$; the letter at $k$ is another $V$, hence $j\leq b-1$. Delete the letter at position $k$ to obtain $\bar w$. This is exactly the prescribed collapse, and its letter counts are $(a,b-1)$.

proof.text: For $k=0$ remove the initial $V$ and put $j=0$; for $k=n$ remove the terminal $V$ and put $j=b$. Again the remaining counts are $(a,b-1)$. Thus all three rules define a map into $\{0,\ldots,b\}\times W_{a,b-1}$, and their $j$ ranges are disjoint.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written word calculation supplying the vertical part of the universal shuffle boundary formula; the blueprint supplies the application only. Weibel §8.5 is WANTED, not a consulted source.

proof.text: For a target $(j,\bar w)$ with $0<j<b$, the word $\bar w$ has at least $j$ letters $V$. Let $p$ be the position of its $j$-th $V$ (counted from one). Replace that letter by $VV$ and mark $k=p+1$. Then $0<k<n$, both adjacent letters are $V$, and $B_k(w)=j$. Collapsing deletes the second of these two letters and recovers $\bar w$. Conversely, an interior input has its $j$-th $V$ at position $k-1$; its collapse leaves that occurrence there, so splitting it recovers both $w$ and the mark $k$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written word calculation supplying the vertical part of the universal shuffle boundary formula; the blueprint supplies the application only. Weibel §8.5 is WANTED, not a consulted source.

proof.text: For $j=0$, prepend $V$ and mark $k=0$; for $j=b$, append $V$ and mark $k=n$. Removing the added letter recovers the target, and adding it back recovers every endpoint input. Together with the disjoint ranges and the two inverse identities in the preceding step, this proves the claimed bijection on labeled pairs, even when several marks collapse to the same word.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written word calculation supplying the vertical part of the universal shuffle boundary formula; the blueprint supplies the application only. Weibel §8.5 is WANTED, not a consulted source.

proof.text: Write $v^{(j)}=d_jv$, so $v^{(j)}_r=v_r$ for $r<j$ and $v^{(j)}_r=v_{r+1}$ for $r\geq j$. In an interior case and for $0\leq t\leq n-1$, if $t<k$ then $A_t(\bar w)=A_t(w)$, $B_t(\bar w)=B_t(w)<j$. If $t\geq k$ then $A_t(\bar w)=A_{t+1}(w)$, $B_t(\bar w)=B_{t+1}(w)-1\geq j$. These follow by counting prefixes after deleting the second $V$. Substitution into the formula for $v^{(j)}$ shows that the $t$-th evaluated pair is the original pair at $t$ in the first case and at $t+1$ in the second. This is exactly $d_kz_{u,v}(w)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written word calculation supplying the vertical part of the universal shuffle boundary formula; the blueprint supplies the application only. Weibel §8.5 is WANTED, not a consulted source.

proof.text: At $k=0$, prefix counting gives $A_t(\bar w)=A_{t+1}(w)$ and $B_t(\bar w)=B_{t+1}(w)-1$ for every $0\leq t<n$. Since $(d_0v)_r=v_{r+1}$, the evaluated pair is the old pair at $t+1$. At $k=n$, prefixes through $t<n$ are unchanged and have $B_t(w)\leq b-1$, so $(d_bv)_{B_t(w)}=v_{B_t(w)}$; the evaluated pair is the old pair at $t$. This proves both endpoint string identities.

proof.text: For an interior collapse, identify all retained letter occurrences in their original order. An inversion involving two retained letters is unchanged. The deleted occurrence is $V$, so its inversions are precisely its pairs with later letters $H$. There are $a-i$ such letters, since the first $k$ letters contain $i$ letters $H$ and the deleted letter itself is $V$. Consequently $I(w)=I(\bar w)+a-i$.

proof.text: Deleting the initial $V$ removes precisely its inversions with all $a$ letters $H$, giving $I(w)=I(\bar w)+a$. Deleting the terminal $V$ removes no inversion, giving $I(w)=I(\bar w)$. At the terminal endpoint $k=n=a+b$ by definition.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written word calculation supplying the vertical part of the universal shuffle boundary formula; the blueprint supplies the application only. Weibel §8.5 is WANTED, not a consulted source.

proof.text: In the interior, $I(w)+k=I(\bar w)+(a-i)+(i+j)=I(\bar w)+a+j$. At the initial endpoint the same equality holds with $k=j=0$; at the terminal endpoint it holds with $k=a+b$, $j=b$. Raising $-1$ to these equal exponents yields $s(w)(-1)^k=(-1)^{a+j}s(\bar w)$ in each case.

proof.text: If $b=1$, an interior pair would require two occurrences of $V$, so only the endpoints remain; the inverse uses only $j=0,1$. If $a=0$, no inversion occurs and $k=B_k(w)=j$ at every mark, consistent with all formulas. If $b=0$, there is no $V$ occurrence and hence no vertical labeled pair (also for the empty word). All string comparisons used indices only, with no distinctness assumption on $u$ or $v$. Equal strings give the same basis symbol in the free module of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], so the displayed equalities also hold under that interpretation.
